experience.headline: Laying the 0->1 foundation as the company's first software engineer.
highlights: Joined as the first software engineer and established the company's entire technical foundation.
Partnered with stakeholders across three business divisions to map manual workflows into well-defined deliverables (tracked in ClickUp).
Selected the full technology stack and designed the relational database schema.

experience.headline: MSc thesis in collaboration with Amazon: measuring and mitigating how code-based LLMs memorise their training data, and the privacy and copyright risks it creates.
highlights: Investigated memorization in code-based LLMs (verbatim reproduction of training data driving privacy, PII-leakage and copyright risk). Awarded a distinction (82%).
Evaluated encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder families (CodeBERT, CodeGPT, CodeT5) on CodeSearchNet across four languages (Python, Java, JavaScript, Ruby), 30,000 samples per language.
Designed two data-extraction attacks (masked-token prediction and prefix-suffix generation) and an extended CodeBLEU metric with AST-based privacy components.

Found identifiers and string literals most memorised (up to 79.3% exact match); verbose languages (Java) memorise more than concise ones (Python); 8-bit quantization reduced exact memorization while preserving code quality.
Analysed how Few-Shot Learning shifts the balance between memorization and generalisation.

featured.title: Decentralized Autonomous Vehicle
featured.context: B.E. Final-Year Thesis - MIT, Anna University
featured.blurb: A Raspberry Pi self-driving car that cooperates with no central server. It parses a spoken destination, resolves an offline route across a dual-layer Folium + Google-Earth map, and plans motion with the Haversine formula, while a YOLO/Darknet perception stack detects 205 traffic-sign classes (trained on 97K+ images) and a custom model reads traffic lights at 83% accuracy, rerouting in real time on-device.

featured.title: Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
featured.blurb: Built and benchmarked four German->English translation architectures on a low-resource Europarl subset, from an attentional LSTM baseline to a lexical model and a from-scratch Transformer with multi-head attention. The lexical model won decisively, converging in 53 epochs against the baseline's 99.

featured.title: ANT-BOT: Autonomous Maze-Solving Rover
featured.blurb: A low-cost ESP32-CAM rover that photographs an unknown maze, solves the shortest escape route with Dijkstra's algorithm over the pixel grid, converts it into a turn-by-turn instruction set, and drives it end to end, validated in a Pygame simulation before hardware deployment.

featured.title: RNN vs GRU Language Modelling
featured.blurb: Implemented vanilla RNN and GRU language models from scratch in NumPy (forward pass, backprop and backpropagation-through-time) to study subject-verb agreement. A hidden-state cosine analysis showed the GRU far better preserves long-range syntactic dependencies.

featured.title: Spotify Hit-Song Prediction
featured.blurb: Predicted whether a track would become a lasting chart hit from its audio features alone, across 650K+ rows of Spotify's Top-200. Benchmarked four classifiers plus K-means clustering. Random Forest led decisively, with energy and danceability the strongest drivers of success.

featured.title: Character-Level Language Identification
featured.blurb: Built interpolated character-trigram language models from scratch (preprocessing, add-alpha smoothing and text generation) that identify a document's language purely by perplexity, then extended the study with four neural next-character models. The English model nailed the test document at a fraction of the rivals' perplexity.
